title: A Blueprint for Curing Aging
content: Aging kills ~100,000 people a day - more than any other cause of death combined.  The exact causes of aging have been much discussed, but the most pressing issue with regard to aging appears to be lipofuscin accumulation.  That is, the accumulation of indigestible cellular garbage that needs to be removed from our cells, then the body.  In this piece, I will explain why I think “getting rid of the garbage” should be at least one of our main goals with regard to longevity research for now.  Of course, if cancer strikes before then, it will need to be addressed.  Curative cancer therapy approaches are discussed herein.  I also list the other causes of aging aside from lipofuscin accumulation - and how we can treat them.  The same foundation on which the systemic lipofuscin removal approach is built can be used for treating genetic disorders and acquired illnesses as well.
